meta.title: ecentic for Shopify: sell through AI assistants
meta.description: Connect Shopify, compare products with AI assistants and publish selected listing changes. Send published changes to Merchant Center in a separate sync.

shopify.title: ecentic for Shopify
shopify.description: Connect your store, see why AI assistants choose competitors, and publish selected fixes to Shopify. Send published fixes to Merchant Center when you choose.

sections.title: From catalog to a clearer listing

items.title: Simulate
items.body: Compare selected products with named competitors using ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

items.title: Fix and publish
items.body: Apply creates and publishes a revised title and description. Structured data has a separate publish action and requires the theme app embed.

items.title: Track
items.body: See detected AI referrals and agent visits, by assistant and over time.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes
sections.description: Importing product content does not rewrite it. Connecting also installs the storefront tracking script. Publishing and structured-data updates are explicit actions.

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: Approve Shopify OAuth permissions: read_products, write_products, write_script_tags and read_script_tags. No Shopify Plus requirement is enforced by this connection.
A catalog sync reads up to 10 pages of 250 products: at most 2,500 records per run. A free onboarding scan selects up to 10 products. Paid plan allowances are listed on Pricing.

The connection uses Shopify Admin API access and its rate limits. The sync is bounded by page count; no additional fixed requests-per-minute allowance is promised. Public-only catalog imports cannot publish changes.

sections.title: Set up your store

items.title: Install and approve
items.body: Install the app and approve Shopify’s permissions. Allow a few minutes; authorization and catalog import time vary.

items.title: Choose the comparison
items.body: Select products and named competitors for the first scan. The scan duration depends on the comparison size and model responses.

items.title: Publish the changes you choose
items.body: Use Apply for a revised title and description. Publish structured data separately and enable the theme app embed to show it.

items.title: Connect Google separately
items.body: Link Merchant Center, then explicitly sync published fixes from the Google controls.

sections.note: Tip: connect a Shopify development store first to inspect the flow before publishing changes to a live catalog.

ledger.read: Existing product title and HTML description.
ledger.write: Updated through the Admin API when you choose Apply or an explicit bulk action.

ledger.read: Product information used to build Product JSON-LD.
ledger.write: A separate publish action writes the metafield. The theme app embed must be enabled to render it.

ledger.read: Variant prices and the imported product payload. No separate inventory sync.
ledger.write: Not changed by the listing publish actions.

ledger.read: Existing image URLs and storefront product links.
ledger.write: Not changed; no image generation.

ledger.read: Detected AI referral and agent visit signals.
ledger.write: An onload ScriptTag is installed during connection for visit tracking.

ledger.read: A paid-order webhook is attempted for attribution where available; no order-history import.
ledger.write: No Shopify order creation or editing.

faqs.question: Does ecentic change product content without asking?
faqs.answer: No. Listing content changes require Apply or an explicit bulk action. Structured data is published separately. Connecting does install the tracking script, so connection is not a promise of zero changes to the store configuration.

faqs.question: Why use ecentic if Shopify already distributes my catalog?
faqs.answer: Catalog distribution and product quality are different jobs. ecentic compares selected listings with competitors and lets you publish changes to the data you control. It does not guarantee recommendations in any channel.

faqs.question: Can I connect Google Merchant Center?
faqs.answer: Yes, for Shopify stores. Use the separate Google sync control to send published title and description overrides plus selected checkout attributes. Clicking Apply on a listing does not automatically sync Google.

faqs.question: How does the tracking script load?
faqs.answer: Shopify installs it with its onload event. The script detects supported referral or agent signals and sends a small beacon to ecentic. We have not measured a universal performance impact and do not claim zero overhead.

meta.title: ecentic for WooCommerce: sell through AI assistants
meta.description: Install the free ecentic WooCommerce plugin to compare products with competitors, publish listing updates, and let compatible AI agents check out in your store.

woocommerce.title: ecentic for WooCommerce
woocommerce.description: Install the free plugin, compare your products with competitors, publish selected fixes and let supported AI agents check out through your own store.

sections.title: A catalog and checkout agents can use

items.title: Simulate
items.body: Compare your selected products with named competitors on ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

items.title: Fix and publish
items.body: Apply publishes a revised name and description through the WooCommerce REST API. Structured data is a separate action, rendered by the plugin.

items.title: Agent checkout
items.body: Let compatible agents search products, price a real cart and create a WooCommerce order. Your payment gateway handles the payment.

sections.title: You control agent checkout
paragraphs: The plugin publishes a discovery profile at a standard address on your own domain. Cart quotes use WooCommerce stock, tax, shipping and coupon rules. Orders are tagged as agent orders; you remain the seller of record.
Switch checkout on or off, configure an agent allow-list, require signed requests and set rate limits. A blank allow-list permits all supported agents. Signature requirements are optional settings.

By default, the agent creates an unpaid order and the buyer pays through your checkout link. Server-side Stripe payments are optional, off by default and require the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway. Payment secrets stay on your server.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes
sections.description: The plugin and approved REST credentials provide the catalog and order operations needed for your chosen features.

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: The published plugin requires WordPress 6.0+, WooCommerce 7.0+ and PHP 8.0+. Connect from wp-admin, or supply WooCommerce REST keys; publishing requires read/write access.
Catalog sync reads at most 20 pages of 100 products: up to 2,000 records per run. The free onboarding scan selects up to 10 products.

Hosted agent endpoints default to 120 requests per minute, per store and client identity. The merchant can configure the limit. Agent checkout needs the plugin; REST catalog keys alone do not install the checkout surface.
AI visit tracking and ecentic’s Merchant Center sync are not available for WooCommerce today.

sections.title: Set up your store

items.title: Install the plugin
items.body: Install and activate the free plugin from WordPress.org. Activation alone does not contact ecentic.

items.title: Approve in wp-admin
items.body: Connect to ecentic from the plugin settings and approve the connection. No keys to copy in this flow; REST keys are an alternative.

items.title: Run your first comparison
items.body: Choose products and competitors, then run a scan. Set aside a few minutes for setup; catalog and model processing times vary.

items.title: Publish and test checkout
items.body: Apply the listing changes you choose. Enable agent checkout when ready and test your payment flow.

sections.note: Tip: use a staging site first, then run the checkout playground against it before enabling real purchases.

ledger.read: Current name, description and product data.
ledger.write: A revised name and description when you choose Apply or an explicit bulk action.

ledger.read: Existing product facts used to generate Product JSON-LD.
ledger.write: A separate action writes protected product metadata, rendered by the plugin.

ledger.read: Imported catalog data and live cart information.
ledger.write: Listing fixes do not change these fields. Normal checkout can affect stock through WooCommerce.

ledger.read: Real WooCommerce cart calculations and store settings.
ledger.write: Cart sessions and buyer checkout selections through the private bridge.

ledger.read: Agent order status and the buyer details needed to fulfill those orders.
ledger.write: Native WooCommerce orders tagged as agent orders; supported checkout operations can update them.

ledger.read: Payment outcomes and supported payment-method information.
ledger.write: No payment-secret storage in ecentic. The merchant gateway charges the approved payment method or the buyer pays via the store link.

faqs.question: Is the plugin free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Install it free from WordPress.org. ecentic plans apply to simulations and listing features; see Pricing for current terms.

faqs.question: Does ecentic take the payment?
faqs.answer: Your existing gateway takes payment and the order belongs to you. The default flow hands the buyer to your payment page. Optional server-side Stripe payment requires the gateway and its setting to be enabled.

faqs.question: Do you track AI visits on WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. AI visit tracking runs on Shopify today.

faqs.question: Can we turn agent checkout off?
faqs.answer: Yes. Disable it from the plugin settings. You can also restrict agents, require signatures or revoke the connection credentials.

faqs.question: Do we need to change our theme or copy API keys?
faqs.answer: The plugin provides the discovery and bridge features. Approve its connection in wp-admin without copying keys, or use read/write REST keys for catalog publishing. Test any theme or payment setup on staging first.

meta.title: ecentic and Google Merchant Center
meta.description: Send published fixes to Merchant Center, inspect product diagnostics and check the settings Google’s agent checkout needs. For Shopify stores.

googleMerchant.title: Google Merchant Center
googleMerchant.description: Send published listing changes to Google as supplemental product data. Review diagnostics and prepare checkout settings from one place. Available for Shopify stores.

sections.title: Keep Google’s product data ready

items.title: Supplemental data
items.body: Send published title and description changes with a separate sync action. Your main product source is retained.

items.title: Checkout attributes
items.body: Set eligible product checkout attributes and include them in the supplemental sync.

items.title: Product diagnostics
items.body: See Google product issues and whether supplemental changes have taken effect.

items.title: Checkout readiness
items.body: Check account, shipping, return and customer-support settings. Google program enrollment remains a merchant task.

sections.note: Google approved ecentic’s Merchant Center write access in September 2026. This is access approval, not an endorsement.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes
sections.description: The connection requests the Google Content API OAuth scope. Your consent authorizes the account operations below; it does not enroll you in Google checkout.

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: A connected Shopify store and a Merchant Center account you can authorize. The current ecentic connection does not support WooCommerce.
Google OAuth scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content. Select the merchant account and complete the account-linking steps shown in the connection flow.

Matching relies on the Shopify product identity and the Merchant Center offer. Google’s diagnostics and processing determine whether each change is accepted. No fixed sync-completion time is guaranteed.
Published listing changes are sent only when you run the sync action. Background maintenance checks existing overrides and account links; it does not automatically send newly published listing fixes.

sections.title: Connect, review, then sync

items.title: Authorize your Google account
items.body: Open the Google connection for your Shopify store and grant access to the intended Merchant Center account.

items.title: Provision the supplemental source
items.body: Complete the account link and data-source setup. Check the matching products and source priority.

items.title: Choose product changes
items.body: Publish listing updates to Shopify and set any eligible checkout attributes. Review Google’s diagnostics.

items.title: Send the overrides
items.body: Run the separate supplemental sync and verify the processed offer state. Allow for Google processing time.

sections.note: Tip: use a test Merchant Center setup where available and verify a small set of matched offers first.

ledger.read: Account identity, connected sources and their configuration.
ledger.write: Account link requests, an ecentic supplemental source and source-priority rules when provisioned.

ledger.read: Published ecentic listing records and processed Merchant Center offers.
ledger.write: Supplemental title and description overrides on explicit sync.

ledger.field: Price, stock and main product feed
ledger.read: Processed offers needed for matching and diagnostics.
ledger.write: No replacement of the main product source; configured supplemental values take precedence for their fields.

ledger.read: Saved product settings and Google’s processed checkout eligibility.
ledger.write: Selected checkout attributes through the supplemental source.

ledger.read: Account shipping settings, return policies and customer-support details.
ledger.write: Customer-support details or a return policy only through their explicit save actions. No shipping-rate writer.

ledger.read: Product issues and the acceptance state of the overrides.
ledger.write: No edits to Google’s diagnostic decisions.

faqs.question: Will this overwrite our main feed?
faqs.answer: The main data source is retained. ecentic creates a supplemental source and updates its priority in the primary source’s rules. The selected supplemental attributes can therefore replace the effective values Google uses for those fields.

faqs.question: Is it available for WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. ecentic’s Merchant Center integration supports Shopify today.

faqs.question: Does this get us into Google’s checkout program?
faqs.answer: No. Google decides eligibility and approval. ecentic prepares data, checks settings and helps test readiness; enrollment is your separate step.

faqs.question: Does Apply automatically update Google?
faqs.answer: No. Apply publishes the selected store listing change. Use the separate Merchant Center sync action to send published overrides to Google.

meta.title: Use ecentic with a product feed or CSV
meta.description: Import a supported XML or JSON product feed, CSV, or accessible public Shopify or WooCommerce catalog for simulations and audits.

productFeeds.title: Product feeds and CSV
productFeeds.description: Start with product data you can export. Import a supported feed or CSV, or use an accessible public Shopify or WooCommerce catalog, without a direct publishing connection.

items.title: Simulate
items.body: Compare imported products with named competitors using the store-scan models.

items.title: Audit
items.body: Check listing quality and sampled storefront readiness. Use the findings to guide your team’s edits.

items.title: Connect when you need to publish
items.body: Publishing to a store needs a Shopify or WooCommerce connection. Google sync is Shopify-only; agent checkout needs the WooCommerce plugin; tracking runs on Shopify.

sections.title: Formats the importer reads
sections.description: Use the documented shapes below. A file being XML or JSON alone does not make it compatible.

rows.label: XML
rows.value: RSS channel/item or feed/entry product records, including Google Shopping-style product fields.

rows.label: JSON
rows.value: A product array, or an object containing products or items as an array. Supported fields include title, description, price, currency, image, URL, SKU and ID.

rows.label: CSV
rows.value: Comma-separated text, one product per row. Columns: title or name; description; price; image, image_link or image_url; url or link; sku; id.
rows.detail: Rows without a title are skipped. Include a currency code in price, for example 29.99 EUR; a separate CSV currency column is not imported. Avoid embedded line breaks.

rows.label: Feed size
rows.value: XML and JSON downloads are limited to 10 MiB.

rows.label: Store address
rows.value: Accessible public Shopify and WooCommerce catalogs. This is not a universal import for every website.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes
sections.description: An import stores product records in ecentic. It does not change the source feed, file or storefront.

sections.title: Use a supported export
sections.description: The verified platform routes below require column mapping. Native direct connections are a separate feature.

sections.title: Import and compare

items.title: Prepare the file
items.body: Use a supported feed URL or normalize your CSV to the supported column names and comma delimiter.

items.title: Import the catalog
items.body: Connect the feed or upload the CSV. Check titles, prices, currency and product URLs before selecting products.

items.title: Choose the comparison
items.body: Pick up to 10 products for the free onboarding scan and add named competitors.

items.title: Review and re-import
items.body: Use audit findings to update your source system. Re-import when your catalog changes; there is no scheduled feed refresh.

sections.note: Tip: start with a small sample export to check the mapping before importing your catalog.

ledger.read: Supported fields in the feed or CSV. CSV currency can be part of the price value.
ledger.write: Stored as product records in ecentic. The source is not modified.

ledger.field: Images, product URLs, SKU and ID
ledger.read: Supported image URLs, links and identifiers.
ledger.write: Stored in ecentic; no new images or identifiers are generated.

ledger.field: Stock, custom attributes and platform-specific fields
ledger.read: Only fields handled by the importer are used; an arbitrary export schema is not supported.
ledger.write: No write-back to your commerce platform.

ledger.read: Imported product records and accessible storefront samples.
ledger.write: Results in ecentic. No downloadable file of generated listing rewrites is available today.

faqs.question: Is importing a feed read-only?
faqs.answer: It is read-only with respect to your source: ecentic does not change your feed, file or storefront. It does save the imported product records in your ecentic account.

faqs.question: How often is the feed refreshed?
faqs.answer: Re-import whenever the catalog changes. Scheduled feed refresh is not available today.

faqs.question: Can we download the fixes as a file?
faqs.answer: There is no export of generated listing rewrites today. Use the audit findings to guide edits in your source system, or connect Shopify or WooCommerce for supported publishing actions.

faqs.question: Does any XML or JSON export work?
faqs.answer: No. The parser accepts the product record shapes listed above. Export formats with different structures must be converted first. CSV column mapping is usually the simplest route.
